page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the DLDSv5 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores running at 2.8 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 614 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations position this server in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores are 1899.08 and 15528.25 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 9941.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 840.03 GB/sec, dropping to 102.63 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in LLM text generation using a small 135M model, achieving 274.55 tokens/sec, which falls into the top 25% tier.

The primary tradeoff of the D16lds_v5 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications but increases cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space, reducing reliance on external storage for temporary files. This hardware profile is suitable for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, lightweight database operations, and small-scale language model inference.
